Both acetylcholine and Arecoline are known to interact with the Proteasome subunit beta type-5, indicating a possible pathway through which brompheniramine may influence this target. The scores from the two paths, while slightly different, both point to a consistent biological link, suggesting that brompheniramine may modulate the activity of the Proteasome subunit beta type-5 via its interaction with these intermediate targets. The evidence supports a mechanistic connection, though the exact nature of the interaction remains to be elucidated.
